TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Canonical Flow Inference
description: Systematic generation of tailored inference algorithms and quantum decoders Canonical Flow Inference, developed at Los Alamos National Laboratory, provides a systematic framework for generating inference algorithms tailored to the mathematical structure of a problem. Starting from its factor graph, the framework constructs the corresponding exact statistical theory, reduces it to an effective theory that retains the relevant qualitative structure, and derives a canonical inference algorithm. For quantum error correction, the framework takes a code and its circuit-level noise model as inputs and generates a decoder tailored to the physical implementation and its correlated error processes. An initial application to quantum color codes achieved approximately twice the error threshold and about fifteen times fewer logical errors at a tested subthreshold operating point than restriction decoding on the same proof-of-principle circuit-noise problem. These simulation results were confirmed across several code-block sizes, suggesting the potential for more reliable, logical qubits and reduced physical-qubit requirements. The derived decoder is a local message-passing algorithm by construction, providing the fast, parallelizable computational structure sought for real-time decoding. Full hardware timing remains to be measured. The Challenge The central difficulty in approximate inference is finding algorithms that remain computationally tractable without losing the correlations and structural constraints that matter to the problem. Quantum error correction makes this particularly concrete: fault-tolerant quantum computing requires both reliable storage and reliable, logical operations. Color codes are attractive because they support efficient fault-tolerant Clifford operations and resource-efficient approaches to magic-state preparation. Magic states supply a resource needed for operations beyond the Clifford gate set. Color-code components may therefore be valuable even in machines that use other codes for most of their computation. Google has demonstrated color-code error suppression and logical operations on superconducting hardware. The practical challenge is decoding: a classical processor must infer a recovery from error-check measurements accurately and fast enough to support the quantum computation. Circuit operations and imperfect measurements create correlations that differ from idealized independent-qubit noise. A decoder that performs well for the ideal code may lose substantial accuracy when applied to the physical circuit. Consequently, even when the code itself is well understood, there remains the problem of obtaining a decoder matched to its physical implementation without sacrificing the speed needed for real-time operation. Problems Solved Canonical Flow Inference provides a systematic procedure for generating inference algorithms directly from the mathematical structure of a problem. The factor graph defines an exact statistical field theory, which can then be reduced to a tractable effective theory while preserving the relevant qualitative structure of the original problem. From this effective theory, the framework derives a canonical inference algorithm, whose rules are determined by the structure of the underlying inference problem rather than being chosen heuristically or ad hoc. For quantum error correction, this means that the code and its physical noise model jointly determine the derived decoder. Applied to the idealized color code, the method produces a decoder from which the standard restriction decoder follows as an approximation. When circuit-level noise is incorporated, however, the factor graph changes, and the resulting decoder changes with it to account for the correlated errors generated by the physical circuit. In the proof-of-principle benchmark, this produced markedly better decoding performance than restriction decoding on the same circuit-level noise problem. How the Approach Differs Conventional decoding approaches generally begin with a chosen class of algorithms, such as belief propagation, matching, or neural networks, and adapt them to a particular code and noise model. Canonical Flow Inference instead derives the algorithm from the effective statistical theory of the inference problem itself. This construction can recover familiar algorithms under suitable approximations but also generates different rules when the underlying problem or its physical noise structure changes. The distinction is therefore not simply the ability to account for correlations or perform calculations in parallel, but the systematic generation of algorithms tailored to the problem being solved. The distinctions above concern how the algorithms are constructed. Comparative performance against newer matching and neural decoders remains to be established through matched benchmarks. Advantages Tailored inference algorithms (the framework systematically generates algorithms adapted to the mathematical structure of a particular problem) More operating margin (increased decoding threshold means that, under the tested circuit-noise model, increasing code size can suppress logical errors across a wider range of physical error rates) Better protected information (fewer logical errors allow longer reliable computations on the same hardware) A path to real-time decoding (derived color-code decoder is a local message-passing algorithm by construction, allowing updates across the factor graph to be carried out in parallel) Circuit and decoder co-design (decoder is derived from the physical circuit and its noise model so the framework could also help optimize gate schedules and auxiliary-qubit arrangements to produce errors that are easier to decode) Market Applications Quantum computing and quantum information processing High-performance computing and specialized computing hardware Digital communications and data storage TRL 3 US Patent pending LA-UR-26-29806 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: Launchpad Infrastructure Project
description: Overview The Idaho National Laboratory (INL) is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified contractors, construction firms, and infrastructure service providers capable of supporting a forthcoming infrastructure development project known as the Launchpad Infrastructure Project. This EOI is being issued for market research purposes only to identify capable organizations, assess regional capacity, and better understand the availability of qualified resources to execute the work within an accelerated project schedule. Responses will help INL evaluate supplier interest, experience, and capability prior to any future procurement activities. Project Description The Launchpad Infrastructure Project is anticipated to support future site development activities through the installation and construction of critical infrastructure components. The project may include but is not limited to the following: Construction of approximately 2 to 3 miles of 2 lane roadway Installation of approximately 2 to 3 miles of water main Installation and routing of approximately 3 miles of fiber conduit and handholes Potential construction of approximately 1 mile of chip seal roadway improvements The final scope, quantities, and project requirements are subject to change as planning and design efforts progress. Anticipated Schedule INL currently anticipates project mobilization and construction activities to begin in March or April 2027. Due to programmatic requirements, the project is expected to operate under a compressed schedule, making contractor availability, resource capacity, and schedule flexibility key considerations. Requested Information Interested organizations are requested to provide the following information: Company name and primary point of contact. Brief description of company capabilities relevant to the anticipated scope. Experience performing similar infrastructure projects involving roadway construction, utility installation, and/or fiber optic infrastructure. Description of available resources, personnel, equipment, and subcontractor relationships that could support a project of this size and schedule. Confirmation of anticipated availability during the March-April 2027 timeframe. Identification of any specialized expertise related to: Roadway construction Water utility installation Fiber optic infrastructure installation Chip sealing operations Any potential constraints, risks, or schedule considerations that may impact project execution. Minimum Qualifications Interested organizations should be able to demonstrate: Relevant experience performing comparable civil infrastructure projects. Ability to manage multiple infrastructure work scopes concurrently. Adequate staffing, equipment, and project management resources to support an accelerated schedule. Compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations. Ability to perform work within a secure and safety-focused operating environment. Important Notice This EOI is issued for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment by INL to award a contract. Any future procurement related to this effort will be announced through appropriate procurement channels. Response Deadline Interested parties are requested to submit their responses no later than end of business day January 15th, 2027. Submission Instructions Please submit responses electronically to: Chase Egbert chase.egbert@inl.gov Questions regarding this EOI may be directed to the contact listed above. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

Dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä: Lääkevalmisteet ja niihin rinnastettavat tuotteet
description: Tällä ilmoituksella perustetaan dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä (Dynamic Purchasing System; DPS). Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän (DPS) kohteena ovat HUSin ja muiden mukana olevien hankintayksiköiden tarvitsemat Lääkevalmisteet ja niihin rinnastettavat tuotteet. Hankittavat lääkevalmisteet ja niihin rinnastettavat tuotteet määritellään tarkemmin kussakin dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisessä kilpailutuksessa. Pyydämme osallistumishakemuksia lääkevalmisteiden ja niihin rinnastettavien tuotteiden dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään otetaan mukaan kaikki soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttävät ehdokkaat. Varsinaiset hankinnat tehdään dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisillä kilpailutuksilla. 30.1.2023 TEHTY SEURAAVAT MUUTOKSET: Tarjoajan osallistumisvaatimuksista on poistettu vaatimus toiminnan vastuuvakuutuksesta. Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän päivämääriä on muutettu. Pyydämme osallistumishakemuksia lääkevalmisteiden ja niihin rinnastettavien tuotteiden dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään (DPS). Hankinnan kohteena dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisällä ovat lääkevalmisteet ja niihin rinnastettavat tuotteet. Tämän dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän ulkopuolelle jäävät sellaiset HUS Apteekin kilpailutukset, joissa hankintarengas on laajempi ja muodostetaan useampien hankintayksiköiden (esim. kaikki Suomen hyvinvointialueet) kesken (esimerkkeinä HIV-lääkkeiden kilpailutus, Hepatiitti-C:n hoitoon tarkoitettujen interferonivapaiden valmisteiden kilpailutus). Tämän dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän ulkopuolelle jäävät myös Radiofarmaseuttisten valmisteiden sekä Lääkkeellisten, teollisten ja muiden sairaalakaasujen kilpailutukset. DYNAAMISEN HANKINTAJÄRJESTELMÄN OSALLISTUMISHAKEMUKSET Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän osallistumishakemukset lähetetään Cloudian Tarjouspalvelussa (https://www.tarjouspalvelu.fi). Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään voi hakea ehdokkaaksi, jos täyttää soveltuvuusvaatimukset, jotka on ilmoitettu ESPD-lomakkeessa sekä kohdassa "Muut ehdot". Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään otetaan mukaan kaikki soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttävät ehdokkaat. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään voi jättää osallistumishakemuksia koko sen keston ajan. Osallistumishakemusten jättämiselle on DPS:n perustamisvaiheessa varattu aikaa 30 vuorokautta (24.2.2023 saakka) siten, että siihen mennessä toimitetut hyväksytyt osallistumishakemukset ehtivät ensimmäiseen sisäiseen kilpailutukseen, jonka tarjouspyyntöä ei julkaista ennen 3.3.2023. Vain ehdokkaat, jotka on hyväksytty Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään, voivat jättää tarjouksia DPS:n sisäisiin kilpailutuksiin. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään hyväksytyt ehdokkaat voivat osallistua yhteen tai useampaan dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäiseen kilpailutukseen. DYNAAMISEN HANKINTAJÄRJESTELMÄN KESTO Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kesto on 16.1.2023-16.1.2027 (48 kuukautta) Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän hankintavaihe alkaa perustamisvaiheen jälkeen, aikaisintaan 3.3.2023. Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän hankintavaihe päättyy dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän voimassaoloajan päättyessä 16.1.2027. Dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä voidaan tilapäisesti sulkea esim. kesälomakauden ajaksi. DPS:n sulkemisesta ilmoitetaan tarvittaessa tarjoajille erikseen. Osallistumishakemuksia ei käsitellä dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän ollessa suljettuna. DYNAAMISEN HANKINTAJÄRJESTELMÄN SISÄISET KILPAILUTUKSET Varsinaiset hankinnat tehdään dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisillä kilpailutuksilla, joissa kuvataan ja täsmennetään hankinnan kohde. HUS voi alkaa julkaista sisäisten kilpailutusten tarjouspyyntöjä hankintavaiheen alettua 3.3.2023. Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisten kilpailutusten tarjouspyynnöissä kuvataan kuhunkin sisäiseen kilpailutukseen kuuluvat lääkevalmisteet ja niihin rinnastettavat tuotteet sekä niiden tarkemmat vertailu- ja valintaperusteet. Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisten kilpailutusten tarjouspyynnöt julkaistaan KILPO kilpailutusportaalissa (https://www.kilpo.fi). Tarjoukset jätetään KILPO kilpailutusportaaliin. Tieto uuden sisäisen kilpailutuksen käynnistymisestä välitetään kaikille dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään hyväksytyille ehdokkaille Cloudian Tarjouspalvelun (https://www.tarjouspalvelu.fi) kautta.

Supply Blanket Purchase Agreement (Hardware)
description: This synopsis is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for quote and no solicitation exists. The Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC), Fort Drum, NY is seeking multiple businesses willing to enter into a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for supplies under North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) 333998: All Other Miscellaneous General Purpose Machinery Manufacturing. The small business size standard for this industry is 700 employees. The Contractor shall supply general hardware and lumber items for the Department of Public works on Fort Drum NY. The Contractor must be located within a 30 mile radius of Fort Drum. The Contractor must be able to accept the Government Purchase Card (GPC). Calls over the $10,000 limit may be paid through Wide Area Workflow (WAWF). To register and access WAWF, go to https://wawf.eb.mil/. There will be times when the Government will utilize Unison Global in order to compete the calls. The Contractor shall register with Unison Global once the Master Blanket Purchase Agreement is signed. The website to register is http://www.unisonglobal.com/, email:info@fedbid.com, phone: 877-933-3243 BPAs will be evaluated annually and may remain in place for up to five years. When establishing these BPAs the Government will consider: Price; Socio-economic status; past performance, where past performance information exists; and technical capabilities. As prescribed in FAR 52.204-7, interested parties must be registered and current in the System for Award Management (SAM), representations and certifications must also be on record. These registrations can be done through the System for Award Management (SAM) for free at http://www.sam.gov/portal/public/SAM/. SAM registration must be complete prior to entering into a BPA. Any interested party may inquire with the following Contract Specialists via email: samara.e.johnson.civ@army.mil, jeffery.l.frans.civ@army.mil, and ernie.a.ixtlahuac.civ@army.mil.
